ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a shaded parallelogram in 3D coordinates. Its labeled vertices are (0,0,0), (0,a,0), (a,0,a), and (a,a,a). The y-axis runs along the bottom edge, the z-axis is vertical, and the x-axis is slanted. The shaded area is the parallelogram spanning these four points. Reasoning: Parametrize the shaded surface using the vertices as \(\vec r(s,t)=(s,t,s)\), with \(0\le s\le a\) and \(0\le t\le a\). The tangent vectors are \(\vec r_s=(1,0,1)\) and \(\vec r_t=(0,1,0)\). To choose the oriented area element with positive x-component, use \(\vec r_t\times \vec r_s=(1,0,-1)\). Thus \(d\vec A=(1,0,-1)\,ds\,dt\). The field is \(\vec E=E_0\hat x=(E_0,0,0)\), so \(\vec E\cdot d\vec A=E_0\,ds\,dt\). Integrating over the square parameter domain gives \(\Phi=\int_0^a\int_0^a E_0\,dt\,ds=E_0a^2\).

method.method_draft: Use the projection rule for flux in a uniform field. From the image, the shaded parallelogram has y ranging from 0 to a and z ranging from 0 to a, while x equals z along the slanted direction. Since the electric field from the text points along +x, only the component of the surface area projected onto the plane perpendicular to x matters, i.e. the yz-plane. The projection of the shaded parallelogram onto the yz-plane is a rectangle/square with side lengths a in y and a in z. Therefore the flux magnitude is E0 times this projected area, E0 a^2, with positive sign for the surface normal chosen along +x.
